```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(readxl)
library(here)
library(janitor)
```

This .Rmd script file was used to create Figure 1 in the 2026 peer-reviewed paper in Nature by Sühring et al., entitled "Multi-Analytical Chemical Fingerprinting: A Method to Establish Contaminant Profiles and Sources of Microplastic Pollution in the Environment."

## Borrowed Code from 'fig_coarse_heatmap.R'

Wrangles Coastal Cleanup Day and CA Ocean Conservancy data to create a dataframe that lists annual counts of plastic debris coarse categories, and calculates each category's rank each year of collection.

```{r}
# load in Coastal Cleanup Day and CA Ocean Conservancy data, as well as the coarse category crossover table data
ccd_raw <- read_excel(here("data", "raw", "Coastalcleanupday_data.xlsx"))
oc_raw <- read_excel(here("data", "raw", "OceanConservancy_CA.xlsx"), 
                     col_types = c("numeric", "text", "text", "text", "text", 
                                   "text", "date", "text", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                   "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric"))
coarse_raw <- read_excel(here("data", "processed", "coarse_data_relational_table.xlsx"))



## reduce oc data to ccd dates ----
ccd_dates <- c("2016-09-17", "2017-09-16", "2018-09-15", "2019-09-21", "2021-09-19")
ccd_dates <- as.Date(ccd_dates)
oc_use <- oc_raw %>%
  mutate(`Cleanup Date` = as.Date(`Cleanup Date`)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(`Cleanup Date` %in% ccd_dates | 
                  (`Cleanup Date` >= as.Date('2020-09-01') & `Cleanup Date` <= as.Date('2020-09-30')))
levels(as.factor(oc_use$`Cleanup Date`)) ## double check

## clean outliers from oc data ----
# see explore_outliers_OCdata.qmd for details
## remove unidentifiable pieces
oc_use <- oc_use |>
  dplyr::rename("Fishing Nets" = "Fishing Net & Pieces") |>
  dplyr::select(-ends_with(c("(Clean Swell)", "Pieces", "Collected"))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Fishing Net & Pieces" = "Fishing Nets") |>
  dplyr::filter(!if_all(15:57, is.na))  ## removes ~1600 cleanups

## remove collected item:people ratio less than one, as well as 0s. Remove cols use to calculate these, if desired 
oc_use <- oc_use |>
  dplyr::mutate(total_collected = rowSums(across(15:57), na.rm = TRUE),
                ratio_collected = round(total_collected/People, 4)) |>
  relocate(ratio_collected, .after = People) |>
  dplyr::filter(ratio_collected > 0.9999) |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(ratio_collected)) |>
  dplyr::select(-total_collected, -ratio_collected)

# wrangle CCD_raw data to long ----
## subset relational table for unique ccd plastic items only ----
coarse_ccd <- coarse_raw |>
  dplyr::select(ccd_coarse_name, used_coarse_name) |>
  distinct() |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ccd_coarse_name))

## make ccd data long & join coarse names ----
ccd_edit <- ccd_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(1,3:30) %>% ## remove 2016 and 2017, use oc data instead
  dplyr::filter(Item != "total") %>%
  remove_empty(which = "rows") %>%
  pivot_longer(!Item, names_to = "Year", values_to = "Count") %>%
  left_join(coarse_ccd, by = c("Item" = "ccd_coarse_name"))

## examine & remove Item without a used_coarse_name ----
## NOTE: this currently assumes Take Out/Away Containers are included in Food Wrappers/Containers; see Issue 4 in repo
ccd_edit |> dplyr::filter(is.na(used_coarse_name)) |> distinct(Item) |> print(n=25)
ccd_edit <- ccd_edit |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(used_coarse_name))

## combine 2 ccd categories ----
### sum Oil/Lube Bottles & Bleach/Cleaner Bottles/Other Plastic Bottles
sum_ccd_bottles <- ccd_edit |>
  dplyr::filter(used_coarse_name == "other plastic bottles") |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(Count = sum(Count, na.rm=TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Item = NA,
                used_coarse_name = "other plastic bottles") |>
  dplyr::relocate(Item, Year, Count, used_coarse_name)

### remove Oil/Lube Bottles & Bleach/Cleaner Bottles/Other Plastic Bottles and row_bind sum_ccd_bottles
ccd_edit <- ccd_edit |>
  dplyr::filter(used_coarse_name != "other plastic bottles") |>
  bind_rows(sum_ccd_bottles)


# wrangle OC_use data to long ----
## subset relational table for unique oc plastic items only ----
coarse_oc <- coarse_raw |>
  dplyr::select(oc_name, used_coarse_name) |>
  distinct() |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(oc_name))

## make oc data long & join coarse names ----
## NOTE: this does include take out/away containers as a separate category
colnames(oc_use)
oc_long <- oc_use %>%
  dplyr::select(1,2,7,9,11,15:57) %>% ## keep columns to help calculate effort later
  remove_empty(which = "rows") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("Cleanup ID", "Zone", "Adults", "People", "Cleanup Date"), names_to = "Item", values_to = "Count") %>%
  left_join(coarse_oc, by = c("Item" = "oc_name"))

## examine & remove Item without a used_coarse_name ----
oc_long |> dplyr::filter(is.na(used_coarse_name)) |> distinct(Item) |> print(n=25)
oc_long <- oc_long |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(used_coarse_name))

## create oc_edit to mimic format of ccd_edit ----
colnames(ccd_edit)
colnames(oc_long)
oc_edit <- oc_long |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Count)) |> 
  mutate(Year = year(`Cleanup Date`)) |>
  dplyr::select(Year, Count, used_coarse_name) |>
  group_by(Year, used_coarse_name) |>
  summarize(Count = sum(Count, na.rm=TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(Year > 2015) ## replace ccd 2016 and 2017 with oc 2016 and 2017. 


# combine _edit dfs & rank ----
## create df with all coarse categories and years ----
na_df <- coarse_raw |>
  dplyr::select(used_coarse_name) |>
  distinct() |>
  slice(rep(1:n(), each = 34)) |> ## seq.int(1988:2021) = 34 years
  dplyr::mutate(Year = rep(1988:2021, times = 43)) ## 43 used_coarse_names

## bind data sets, join with blank df, create ranks
fig_df <- ccd_edit |>
  dplyr::select(!Item) |>
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year)) |> ## aid bind_rows
  bind_rows(oc_edit) |>
  right_join(na_df, by = c("Year", "used_coarse_name")) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  mutate(Rank = rank(desc(Count), na.last = "keep", ties.method = "average")) |> ## not certain what ties.method to use
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(desc(Year), Rank)

```

## New Code to create 'fig_coarse_bar_dotwhisker_plots.png' (Figure 1)

### Data Wrangling

```{r}
# take a subset of the dataframe created in the code chunk above, removing data from the year 2021 and only keeping rows of category counts that had a rank between 1-10 (i.e., top 10).
fig_df_subset <- fig_df %>% 
  filter(Year != 2021) %>% 
  filter(Rank < 11)

# view list of categories that appear in top 10 ranking
unique(fig_df_subset$used_coarse_name)
```

```{r}
# sort the data frame and create a factor with labels to use for the graph
# Assuming 'category_var' is your category variable in a data frame called 'data'
fig_df_subset$used_coarse_name <- factor(fig_df_subset$used_coarse_name, 
                                         levels = sort(levels(factor(fig_df_subset$used_coarse_name)), 
                                                       decreasing = TRUE))
labels <- unique(fig_df_subset$used_coarse_name)
labels
```

### Create left side of figure: bar graph

```{r}
## create bar graphs

# wrangle data, summarize counts, create bar graph
# png(here("figures", "Fig1.png"), units="in", width=6, height=4, res=300)
fig_df_subset %>%
  group_by(used_coarse_name) %>%
  summarise(Count = n()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(used_coarse_name,(Count)), y = Count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
  ylab("Years in top 10 rank") +
  xlab("Plastic-inclusive categories") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() 
# dev.off()


### bar graph used in figure 1
# dropping the last 3 categories, since they only show up 1 year in the top 10 rank (i.e., only keeping categories that appear in top 10 rank more than one year)
fig_df_subset_dropped <- fig_df_subset %>% 
  filter(used_coarse_name != "gloves & masks",
         used_coarse_name != "six-pack holders",
         used_coarse_name != "strapping bands") %>% 
  group_by(used_coarse_name) %>%
  summarise(Count = n())
  
bargraph <- fig_df_subset_dropped %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(used_coarse_name,(Count)), y = Count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
  ylab("Years in top 10 rank") +
  xlab("Plastic-inclusive categories") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() 

show(bargraph)
```

### Create right side of figure: box and whisker plot

```{r, warning=FALSE}
## create boxplot

# select subset of data
fig_df_boxplot <- fig_df %>% 
  filter(Year != 2021,
         # dropping the last 3 categories, since they only show up 1 year in the top 10 rank
         used_coarse_name != "gloves & masks",
         used_coarse_name != "six-pack holders",
         used_coarse_name != "strapping bands")

### plot boxplots
## match factor order in histograms
used_coarse_name_f <- factor(fig_df_boxplot$used_coarse_name, 
                             levels = c("bags",
                                        "caps & lids",
                                        "dishes & cutlery",
                                        "food wrappers & containers",
                                        "plastic beverage bottles 2L or less",
                                        "cigarettes & filters",
                                        "straws & stirrers",
                                        "building & construction materials",
                                        "clothing & shoes",
                                        "cigar tips",
                                        "balloons",
                                        "pull tabs",
                                        "tobacco packaging & wrap",
                                        "cigarette lighters",
                                        "other plastic or foam packaging",
                                        "fishing line",
                                        "rope")) 

# png(here("figures", "Fig1_boxplot.png"), units="in", width=6, height=4, res=300)

fig_df_boxplot %>%
  dplyr::filter(used_coarse_name %in% used_coarse_name_f) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(used_coarse_name_f = factor(used_coarse_name, 
                                            levels = c("bags",
                                        "caps & lids",
                                        "dishes & cutlery",
                                        "food wrappers & containers",
                                        "plastic beverage bottles 2L or less",
                                        "cigarettes & filters",
                                        "straws & stirrers",
                                        "building & construction materials",
                                        "clothing & shoes",
                                        "cigar tips",
                                        "balloons",
                                        "pull tabs",
                                        "tobacco packaging & wrap",
                                        "cigarette lighters",
                                        "other plastic or foam packaging",
                                        "fishing line",
                                        "rope"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = used_coarse_name_f, y = Count)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, varwidth = TRUE) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev(levels(used_coarse_name_f))) +
  theme_bw() +
  # theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab("Count, log10 scale") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "bt") +
  coord_flip()
# dev.off()
```

```{r, warning = FALSE}
## dot and whisker boxplot version

# old plot
# png(here("figures", "Fig1_boxplot.png"), units="in", width=6, height=4, res=300)
fig_df_boxplot %>%
  dplyr::filter(used_coarse_name %in% used_coarse_name_f) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(used_coarse_name_f = factor(used_coarse_name, 
                                            levels = c("bags",
                                        "caps & lids",
                                        "dishes & cutlery",
                                        "food wrappers & containers",
                                        "plastic beverage bottles 2L or less",
                                        "cigarettes & filters",
                                        "straws & stirrers",
                                        "building & construction materials",
                                        "clothing & shoes",
                                        "cigar tips",
                                        "balloons",
                                        "pull tabs",
                                        "tobacco packaging & wrap",
                                        "cigarette lighters",
                                        "other plastic or foam packaging",
                                        "fishing line",
                                        "rope"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = used_coarse_name_f, y = Count)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, varwidth = TRUE) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev(levels(used_coarse_name_f))) +
  theme_bw() +
  # theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab("Annual count, log10 scale") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "bt") +
  coord_flip()
# dev.off()

# new plot
fig_summary <- fig_df_boxplot %>% 
  filter(used_coarse_name %in% used_coarse_name_f) %>%
  group_by(used_coarse_name) %>% 
  summarise(median = median(Count, na.rm = TRUE),
            q1 = quantile(Count, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            q3 = quantile(Count, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(used_coarse_name_f = factor(used_coarse_name, 
                                            levels = rev(c("bags",
                                        "caps & lids",
                                        "dishes & cutlery",
                                        "food wrappers & containers",
                                        "plastic beverage bottles 2L or less",
                                        "cigarettes & filters",
                                        "straws & stirrers",
                                        "building & construction materials",
                                        "clothing & shoes",
                                        "cigar tips",
                                        "balloons",
                                        "pull tabs",
                                        "tobacco packaging & wrap",
                                        "cigarette lighters",
                                        "other plastic or foam packaging",
                                        "fishing line",
                                        "rope"))))

### dot and whisker plot used in figure 1
# plot it

dotwhisker <- ggplot(fig_summary,
       aes(y = used_coarse_name_f,
           x = median)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = q1, xmax = q3),
                 height = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1e3, 1e4, 1e5),
                labels = scales::comma) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "bt") +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab("Annual count, log10 scale") +
  ylab(NULL)

show(dotwhisker)
```

### Plot the graphs side by side to create joint graph: Figure 1

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# load package to plot graphs side by side
library(patchwork)

# remove right plot's y-axis labels
dotwhisker <- dotwhisker +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"))

# bold left plot's axis labels
bargraph <- bargraph +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"))

# view both graphs
bargraph + dotwhisker 

# export grouped graphs (Figure 1)
ggsave(filename = "coarse_bar_dotwhisker_plots.png",
       path = here("figures"),
       width = 10,
       dpi = "retina")
```

Figure 1: Representative plastic items found along California beaches during annual Coastal Clean Up Day (1988-2020), informing product selection for multi-analytical chemical fingerprinting. Left: Number of years in which each product category ranked among the top 10 most frequently collected (by count). Categories are included if they ranked in the annual top 10 more than once. Right: Distribution of annual item counts for each product category across all years (median shown as point; horizontal lines denote first and third quartiles).
